pt:prop:manifestation-not-devoid-of-real.formulation: There can be no conscious manifestation (prakāśa) devoid of a realization (vimarśa); the internal manifestation is the Lord because it has pratyavamarśa as its essence.
pt:prop:manifestation-not-devoid-of-real.subject: prakāśa / vimarśa
pt:prop:manifestation-not-devoid-of-real.assumptions: read as Ratié's report of Utpaladeva's own position, not later Śaivism generally

evidence.claim: There can be no conscious manifestation (prakāśa) devoid of a realization (vimarśa); the internal manifestation is none other than the Lord because it has a realization (pratyavamarśa) as its essence.

span.quote: there can be no [conscious] manifestation (prakāśa) devoid of a realization (vimarśa)

evidence.claim: Sanderson reports (Cidvilāsastava) that Śiva and Śakti embody the self-manifest light of reality (prakāśa) and its innate power of creative ideation (vimarśa) as the unitary source.

embodying the self-manifest light of reality (prakasah) and its

alternative_readings.claim: Sanderson (on Tantrāloka 10.269) reports that in the Fourth state the Light of Consciousness is self-manifest; a distinct claim about manifestation than 'manifestation-not-devoid-of-realization'.

span.quote:
the Light of Consciousness is self-manifest and we cannot speak of an 
immersion, except metaphorically

pt:prop:liberation-is-conviction-of-iden.formulation: Liberation is achieved by conviction of one's identity with Śiva; no external cause bestows it.
pt:prop:liberation-is-conviction-of-iden.subject: liberation / recognition of identity
pt:prop:liberation-is-conviction-of-iden.scope: Abhinavagupta / Tantrāloka 15.42-43b, as reported by Sanderson
pt:prop:liberation-is-conviction-of-iden.modality: identity of means (conviction), denial of external cause
pt:prop:liberation-is-conviction-of-iden.temporal_scope: Abhinavagupta / 11th c. Kashmir; reported by Sanderson
pt:prop:liberation-is-conviction-of-iden.assumptions: reported through Sanderson's citation of Tantrāloka; not a claim by Utpaladeva

evidence.claim: Sanderson states (quoting Tantrāloka 15.42-43b) that conviction of one's identity with Śiva is the means of liberation and that no external cause bestows it.

span.quote:
Conviction of 
one's identity with Siva is the means; no external cause bestows liberation

pt:prop:gnosis-is-the-means-of-liberatio.subject: gnosis vs ritual as means of liberation

evidence.claim: Sanderson reports that the inner conviction of identity with Śiva, a form of knowledge, is the real means of liberation.

span.quote:
This 
inner conviction alone, a form of knowledge, is the real means of liberation

liberation through insight alone and recognition as a 
Guru without passing through visible ceremonies

evidence.claim: Goodall et al. report that Utpaladeva argued that an object by nature alien to consciousness is unthinkable, in his polemic against the existence of external objects (Vijñānavādin debate).

span.quote:
an object by nature alien to consciousness is simply 
unthinkable

pt:prop:siva-sakti-footstool-is-consciou.formulation: The (ritual) footstool of Śiva-and-Śakti is identified with consciousness itself.

the footstool on which the [two] feet 
of Siva-and-Sakti rest, identifying it with consciousness itself
